sections.markdown:
## C2 — Confusable pairs and continuation facts: speeding worth two, three or a fixed listed value, advisory versus suspension, the three revocation windows, point suspension lengths versus school bus lengths, suspended versus revoked, and the failure to appear fee
Confusable pairs among the point system rules, plus continuation facts that complete part C; each block ties to one guide page, the bureau's street address, room number and office hours are agency contact details and are not taught, and hint metadata sits only in the trailing line of a block.

FACT_ID: sec13-R01 | anchor: A01
The guide's example says speeding may bring two or three points depending on the court level, while its list of state law violations shows speeding at 3 points. [A01]
Why it matters: group point values; confusable court-level range versus listed state value; difficulty high.
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0075]

FACT_ID: sec13-R02 | anchor: A01
Four points in 12 months brings only an advisory letter; a suspension starts at 8 or more points in 18 months. [A01]
Why it matters: group thresholds; confusable advisory versus suspension; difficulty high.
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0075]

FACT_ID: sec13-R03 | anchor: A01
Across the three revocation thresholds, each step adds 6 points and 12 months: 12 in 12, 18 in 24, and 24 in 36. [A01]
Why it matters: group thresholds; mnemonic for the revocation windows; difficulty medium.
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0075]

FACT_ID: sec13-R04 | anchor: A01
Careless and imprudent driving and knowingly letting an unlicensed person drive carry the same value, 4 points each. [A01]
Why it matters: group point values; confusable equal values; difficulty medium.
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0075]

FACT_ID: sec13-R05 | anchor: A01
The four violations worth 12 points are leaving the scene of a crash, a felony involving a motor vehicle, getting a license by misrepresentation, and driving while suspended or revoked. [A01]
Why it matters: group point values; grouping of the highest values; difficulty medium.
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0075]

FACT_ID: sec13-R06 | anchor: A02
School bus suspensions run 90, 90 and then 180 days, unlike the point suspensions of 30, 60 and 90 days. [A02]
Why it matters: group suspensions; confusable school bus versus point suspension lengths; difficulty high.
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0076]

FACT_ID: sec13-R07 | anchor: A02
The second and third school bus offenses only raise the suspension when they fall within 5 years. [A02]
Why it matters: group suspensions; difficulty medium.
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0076]

FACT_ID: sec13-R08 | anchor: A02
Driving while suspended may lead to a one-year revocation, but driving while revoked can be a felony with another one-year revocation. [A02]
Why it matters: group other consequences; confusable suspended versus revoked; difficulty high.
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0076]

FACT_ID: sec13-R09 | anchor: A02
Point reduction goes one-third after the first clean year, one-half after the second, and zero after the third, so the cuts get larger each year. [A02]
Why it matters: group point reduction; confusable order of fractions; difficulty medium.
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0076]

FACT_ID: sec13-R10 | anchor: A02
The point total is lowered to four at reinstatement, before any yearly reduction begins. [A02]
Why it matters: group point reduction; continuation of reinstatement.
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0076]

FACT_ID: sec13-R11 | anchor: A02
Paying the ticket alone does not end a failure to appear suspension, because the $20 reinstatement fee is also required. [A02]
Why it matters: group failure to appear; difficulty medium.
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0076]

FACT_ID: sec13-R12 | anchor: A02
Details on filing SR-22 proof of insurance are in the mandatory insurance chapter of the guide. [A02]
Why it matters: group reinstatement; cross reference.
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0076]

FACT_ID: sec13-R13 | anchor: A02
For a first school bus offense, the court can set a suspension period other than the standard one. [A02]
Why it matters: group suspensions; continuation of first offense.
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0076]

FACT_ID: sec13-R14 | anchor: A01
Points are tied to convictions: the Department adds them once it is notified that you were convicted of a moving violation. [A01]
Why it matters: group how points are added; difficulty medium.
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0075]
